editorial.headline: When Creative Work Is Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity embraces conceptual art, choreography and fashion styling, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium makes PMA registration unavailable there.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, this is not a Bali registration today. Nationally, however, the activity is open to PMA with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100 per cent. That creates a clear distinction that matters before the creative description is even considered: the national position permits full foreign ownership, while Bali’s province-wide rule blocks PMA registration for this activity. The contrast is not a matter of interpretation or a small procedural hurdle; it determines whether the activity can be registered in Bali by a foreign-owned business now.

At its centre, the activity is about making art: creating conceptual works, developing choreography and working as a fashion stylist, alongside other art-creation work within the stated scope. It is framed for performing-arts creative practitioners, artists and other creative workers whose contribution is the making of the work itself. The boundary is important. The stated scope keeps restoration and conservation work outside it, including furniture restoration other than museum restoration, stained-glass restoration, renovation or restoration of buildings and historic sites, museum operation, and restoration of artworks, textiles, embroidery, decorated interiors, furnace tiles and decorative painting. The description focuses attention on original creative production rather than those listed restoration or institutional activities.

That creative orientation does not confine the activity to one company size. The stated scale range runs from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah to Besar. Its availability is therefore expressed across all four stated scales, rather than being limited in the record to a single size band. The category’s own language brings together performing-arts creative practitioners with other art and creative workers, while its named examples give it a practical centre of gravity: concept-led art, choreography and fashion styling. These are the recorded expressions of the activity’s creative remit.

In Bali, the answer changes completely. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns every scope in this activity a Low or Medium-Low risk classification. Bali’s moratorium, in force from the thirteenth of May 2026, blocks PMA registration for all KBLI in those two risk bands, island-wide and permanently. The record therefore marks this activity as blocked in Bali on risk-class grounds. A national ceiling of 100 per cent remains the national position, but it does not override the Bali moratorium: a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today.
